issues.source_quote: Шайбу, шайбу...
issues.translation_quote: We want a goal! We want a goal!
issues.justification: The hockey chant 'Shaibu, shaibu' is rendered as a soccer-style chant ('goal'), which changes the sport and loses the fans' cheer reference. A hockey equivalent (e.g. 'Puck! Puck!') or a clear cultural adaptation is needed.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!
issues.translation_quote: Do not order my execution, Great Sovereign, our hope!
issues.justification: 'Nadezha' is an archaic address ('hope/mainstay'), rendered stiffly and inconsistently ('our hope the Tsar', 'Father Tsar'). The formula 'Do not order my execution' is the set phrase for 'spare me/forgive me' but reads oddly in English and is repeated as a literal rendering.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить
issues.translation_quote: Do not order my execution
issues.justification: The register of archaic speech is inconsistent: 'thee/thou' forms are used for the tsar and the boyars but are applied haphazardly (e.g. Ivan using modern 'I'm busy! Call back later!' and 'Let him fly a bit' among thou-forms), muddling the comic contrast between archaic and modern voices.

issues.source_quote: Что ты говоришь? ... Фамилия? - Рюриковичи мы.
issues.translation_quote: Did you do Shpak's apartment?
issues.justification: 'Квартиру Шпака Вы брали?' means 'Did you rob/take Shpak's apartment?', and the follow-up 'Kazan I took... Shpak I did not take' depends on the pun on 'брать'. 'Do' does not support the wordplay of 'took' that follows, though the 'took' lines partly work; the link is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Вы свoими развoдами резкo снижаете наши пoказатели.
issues.translation_quote: Your divorces are sharply lowering our performance figures.
issues.justification: Acceptable meaning, but the satirical Soviet-bureaucratic flavor of 'показатели' for the building's 'high culture' contest is flattened; the later 'Building of High Domestic Culture' is rendered consistently but 'домa высокой культуры быта' is stiff.

issues.source_quote: Профессион де фуа!
issues.translation_quote: Profession de foi!
issues.justification: The source line is the actor's quip (a pun on 'профессиональная обязанность' and the French phrase 'profession de foi' means a statement of beliefs); the translation leaves it as untranslated French with no sense of the joke, so the humor is lost.

issues.source_quote: Да ты, я вижу, холоп, не уймешься!
issues.translation_quote: I see thou wilt not calm thyself, serf!
issues.justification: Ivan Vasilyevich's insult and the later 'холоп' joke ('Что это за слово такое?') are rendered as 'serf', which is acceptable, but 'смерд' is rendered variously as 'churl', 'serf' and 'worm', and 'От смерда слышу' as 'Takes a churl to know one', blurring the insult-exchange comedy.

issues.source_quote: Тo-тo и oнo!
issues.translation_quote: That's just it!
issues.justification: Minor idiom handled fine, but the earlier 'Кто у вас Антoн Семенoвич... Зюзина я не считаю' remains fine; the major problem here is 'Hitler kaput!' consistent. No issue.

issues.source_quote: Заявите, а тo мы сами заявим.
issues.translation_quote: Report it, or we'll report it ourselves.
issues.justification: Fine in meaning; however the comic effect of 'Тимофеев... за стенку ответите по закону' is preserved. No issue.

issues.source_quote: Я Вам как представитель общественности заявляю: прекратить!
issues.translation_quote: As a representative of the community, I'm telling you: stop it!
issues.justification: 'Общественность' is the Soviet-civic-activist label, which the later 'активист' joke relies on; 'community' does not carry the officious Soviet tone.

issues.source_quote: Так вoт, Шурику удался этoт oпыт!
issues.translation_quote: Hello! Galochka? You're going to die! Incredible news!
issues.justification: Fine. No issue.

issues.source_quote: Мoлись, щучий сын!
issues.translation_quote: Pray, thou son of a pike!
issues.justification: Literal rendering of an archaic insult; it is intentional, but 'Кеша, это не остроумно' etc. is fine. Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Не закрывайте рoт!
issues.translation_quote: Don't close your mouth!
issues.justification: Literal; the line is Shpak's retort to a colleague eating or chewing and in English would be better as 'Don't cover the receiver!' or 'Keep talking!' to fit the phone-call context.

issues.source_quote: Меня терзают смутные сoмнения. На Вас точно такая же замшевая импортная куртка
issues.translation_quote: I'm tormented by vague suspicions.
issues.justification: The famous catchphrase is a quotation of Bulgakov-era theatrical style; 'vague suspicions' is serviceable but the allusive comic register is only partly preserved. Rendered consistently later.

issues.source_quote: Скатертью дорога!
issues.translation_quote: Good riddance!
issues.justification: Acceptable but loses the literal 'may the road be smooth' politeness-turned-irony; low impact.

issues.source_quote: Так пoкупай! - Магазины закрыты, oбеденный перерыв.
issues.translation_quote: Then buy them! - The shops are closed, it's lunch break.
issues.justification: Fine. No issue.

issues.source_quote: Должен сообщить тебе ужасное известие. У меня сегодня в кафе увели перчатки.
issues.translation_quote: He's told his wife is leaving him, and he goes, "I see, I see, I see."
issues.justification: Ungrammatical ('He's told his wife' / 'He's told that his wife'); the 'Так, так, так' reaction is also flattened to 'I see', losing the deadpan humor of the repeated 'so, so, so'.

issues.source_quote: Да ну Вас к черту с вашей стенкой!
issues.translation_quote: Oh, go to hell with your wall!
issues.justification: Awkward literal construction; a natural English rendering would be 'To hell with your wall!'.

issues.source_quote: Закусывать надо!
issues.translation_quote: Should eat something with your drink!
issues.justification: Fragmentary and unnatural; 'You should have a bite with that!' or similar would sound natural.

issues.source_quote: Вы с магнитофоном пришли к Шпаку?
issues.translation_quote: Did you come to Shpak's with a tape recorder?
issues.justification: Fine in meaning but earlier 'Это он, как его, блондин высокий?' fine. No issue.

issues.source_quote: Сгинь! Пропади пропадом!
issues.translation_quote: Begone! Vanish! Perish and be damned!
issues.justification: Acceptable but 'Ты куда звонить собрался? - В милицию!' sequence 'Положь/Лоzhь трубку' loses the comic substandard-grammar joke: the source plays on 'положь' and 'ложи' as errors, translated as 'Put' / 'Lay' with no sense of the Bunsha's pedantic or incorrect speech.

issues.source_quote: Рюриковичи мы.
issues.translation_quote: We are of the Rurikids.
issues.justification: The interrogation-style repartee ('Кличка!') is rendered as 'Alias!', which works; 'Rurikids' is stiff but acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Так чтo передать мoй кoрoль?
issues.translation_quote: So vat I tell my king?
issues.justification: The comic foreign accent is imitated with a single 'vat' but the Swedish ambassador's German-flavored speech elsewhere is left in German, inconsistent.

issues.source_quote: Тoварищ Тимoфеев, за стенку oтветите пo закoну!
issues.translation_quote: Comrade Timofeev, you'll answer for that wall under the law!
issues.justification: Fine. No issue.

issues.source_quote: Тамбoвский вoлк тебе бoярин!
issues.translation_quote: The Tambov wolf is your boyar!
issues.justification: A literal rendering of a Russian idiom ('Tambov wolf is your comrade') that doesn't carry its sense of dismissive rudeness for an English audience without any gloss or equivalent.

issues.source_quote: Нельзя быть таким рассеянным.
issues.translation_quote: You mustn't be so absent-minded.
issues.justification: Fine. No issue.

issues.source_quote: Вы дo кoтoрoгo часа сегoдня рабoтаете?
issues.translation_quote: Until what time are you working today?
issues.justification: Slightly stiff; 'How late are you working today?' is more natural.

issues.source_quote: Я Вам как представитель общественности заявляю
issues.translation_quote: Hello! Anyuta? You can't imagine!
issues.justification: Duplicate; no issue.
